title: The World Ratings
audit_comment: THE WORLD RATING TABLES of DMO Chapter 2 (printed pp. 46-54): Table 2 the chronological ratings (the 17-row local-time grid, the fast 9-or-less and slow 13-or-more thresholds, the locality doctrine), Table 3 the magical ratings (the 17-row ladder of max spell level, casting multiplier, and modified schools; the spellbook-free and study-free tiers; the demihuman and fantastic deprivation bands; the item-decay and priest-planar doctrines), Table 4 the technological ratings (the eight era thresholds from steel to FTL, the device-decay doctrine, the advanced-tech margin), Table 5 the ecological ratings (the 3x3 condition grid, the hazard and paradise bands, the native intolerance), and the quirks doctrine.
audit_anchor: // ---- R227: the wis mental save wiring audit ----
prev_record: the spec also seats the R600

banner.title: THE WORLD RATINGS - DMO Chapter 2 continues: Table 2 the chronological ladder (one local week = one base second on C2, one hundred base years on C20; visitors age at local time, spell durations local), Table 3 the magical ladder (dead magic at M2, the ninth-level bar at M8, spellbooks-free at M19, study-free at M20; demihumans save vs. death at M5-or-less, fantastic penalties from M6; items lose one plus per plane, four planes the maximum span), Table 4 the technological ladder (steel at 10-12 through FTL at 20; high-tech devices go inert low, advanced tech works like magic at a five-point margin), Table 5 the ecological grid (constitution, damage, and the poison save at severe, hostile, and deadly), and the world quirks (the Ravenloft infusion, the Athas metal bar, the named-spell bar, the dominant-race retaliation at M14+, the distance-immune world).
banner.provenance: verified against printed pp. 46-54 of the uploaded DMO session capture (part 1, printed page N at OCR page N+1); Table 2 from p. 46, Table 3 from pp. 46-47, Table 4 from pp. 51-52, Table 5 and the quirks from pp. 52-54; the Table 2 and Table 3 rows carry the printed magnitude and unit codes (the engine grids are numeric); the Table 4 prose ladder pins as the eight era-threshold consts per the R595 ladder precedent.
banner.sentinel: the gap census after this round: 19 closed, 77 open - the rating tables and the quirks are closed; the monster-doctrine boxes (the +/-1/2/3 modifier doctrine and Tables 6-22) follow.

consts.name: delChronoCount
consts.comment: the chronological grid row count: 17 rows spanning the ratings C2 through C20, the 10-12 band as one row (printed p. 46, Table 2).

consts.name: delMagicCount
consts.comment: the magical grid row count: 17 rows spanning the ratings M2 through M20, the 10-12 band as one row (printed pp. 46-47, Table 3).

consts.name: delEcologyCount
consts.comment: the ecological condition grid row count: three conditions - constitution loss, damage, and the poison save - each at severe, hostile, and deadly intensity (printed p. 54, Table 5).

consts.name: delChronoFastMax
consts.comment: the fast-time threshold: in worlds rated 9 or less time flows more quickly than the base campaign - travelers return home to find almost no time has passed (printed p. 46).

consts.name: delChronoSlowMin
consts.comment: the slow-time threshold: in worlds rated 13 or more time flows more slowly - travelers return to find their world greatly changed after even a short visit (printed p. 46).

consts.name: delMagicNoNinthMax
consts.comment: the ninth-level bar: no character can cast a 9th-level spell on a world rated M8 or lower; stored spells and items are the exception (printed p. 48).

consts.name: delMagicSpellbookFreeMin
consts.comment: the spellbook-free tier: on worlds rated M19 or higher wizards do not require spellbooks - after a good night's sleep they meditate and acquire any available spell, just as priests do (printed p. 51).

consts.name: delMagicStudyFreeMin
consts.comment: the study-free tier: on M20 worlds wizards and priests do not require study time at all - they call spells to mind as needed, still limited by spells per day and components (printed p. 51).

consts.name: delDemihumanDeathSaveMax
consts.comment: the demihuman bar: demihumans (elves, gnomes, dwarves, orcs, ogres, and similar) must save vs. death magic immediately when entering worlds rated M5 or less - failure is death (printed p. 52).

consts.name: delDemihumanMaxPenalty
consts.comment: the demihuman deprivation maximum: -4 on an M2 world - the penalty grows one point per rating below 5, with the hit-point loss floored at one point per hit die (printed p. 52).

consts.name: delFantasticPenaltyStartMax
consts.comment: the fantastic-creature bar: fantastic creatures (centaurs, dragons, chimeras, pixies, tanar'ri and others) suffer similar penalties beginning on worlds rated M6 (printed p. 52).

consts.name: delFantasticMaxPenalty
consts.comment: the fantastic deprivation maximum: -5 on an M2 world (printed p. 52).

consts.name: delItemPlusLossPerPlane
consts.comment: the item decay: magical weapons, armor, and protective devices are attuned to their world of making and lose one plus per plane removed from home - all Prime Material worlds share one plane (printed p. 52).

consts.name: delMaxPlaneDistance
consts.comment: the planar span: the maximum distance between planes is four - Inner Plane to Ethereal to Prime Material to Astral to Outer Plane; the Astral and Ethereal are one removed from the Prime, the Inner and Outer two (printed p. 52).

consts.name: delPspUnaffectedMin
consts.comment: the psionic high-magic tier: on worlds rated M13 or greater psionics are unaffected, though some worlds - the Demiplane of Ravenloft - have quirks that reach even psionics (printed p. 51).

consts.name: delPriestLossPerPlane
consts.comment: the open-world divine agreement: priests lose one level of spellcasting ability for every plane they are removed from their deity's home plane - a 10th-level priest one plane away casts as 9th (printed p. 49).

consts.name: delPriestCelestiaAbyssLoss
consts.comment: the great-ring worked example: a priest whose deity resides on Mount Celestia and who visits the Abyss loses seven levels of spellcasting ability, tracing the path along the ring (printed p. 50).

consts.name: delMajorRaceMinorMin
consts.comment: the major-race minor tier: minor abilities (similar to 1st-2nd level spells, usable 1-3 times a day) function on worlds rated M7 or higher (printed p. 52).

consts.name: delMajorRaceMajorMin
consts.comment: the major-race major tier: major abilities (similar to 3rd-5th level spells) function on worlds rated M8 or higher, the creature also carrying 4-6 minor abilities usable once a turn or once an hour (printed p. 52).

consts.name: delMajorRaceExtraordinaryMin
consts.comment: the major-race extraordinary tier: extraordinary abilities (similar to 6th-7th level spells, once a day) function on worlds rated M9 or higher, with 6-10 minor abilities at will and 4-6 major abilities once a turn or hour (printed p. 52).

consts.name: delNaturalMinorMax
consts.comment: the natural spellcasting bands: minor spellcasting is 1st-3rd level (printed p. 50).

consts.name: delNaturalMajorMax
consts.comment: the natural spellcasting bands: major spellcasting is 4th-7th level (printed p. 50).

consts.name: delNaturalExtraordinaryMax
consts.comment: the natural spellcasting bands: extraordinary spellcasting is 8th-11th level - the abilities retained when visiting lower-rated worlds, though casting times extend and high levels still become unavailable (printed p. 50).

consts.name: delTechSteelMin
consts.comment: the tech ladder, the steel rung: ratings of 10-12 indicate the medieval technology common to most AD&D campaigns - steel tools and weapons, coal mining, trade and craft guilds, small slow sailing ships, feudal governments, extensive trade (printed pp. 51-52, Table 4).

consts.name: delTechFirearmMin
consts.comment: the tech ladder, the firearm rung: cannons and ocean-going sailing ships arrive at 13; firearms, printing, and intercontinental trade at 14 (printed p. 52, Table 4).

consts.name: delTechSteamMin
consts.comment: the tech ladder, the steam rung: steam engines, blast furnaces, and mechanical calculating machines at 15 (printed p. 52, Table 4).

consts.name: delTechCombustionMin
consts.comment: the tech ladder, the combustion rung: internal combustion engines, light aircraft, steamships, railroads, and labor unions at 16 (printed p. 52, Table 4).

consts.name: delTechNuclearMin
consts.comment: the tech ladder, the nuclear rung: nuclear power, civil and military aircraft, and electronic computers at 17 (printed p. 52, Table 4).

consts.name: delTechFusionMin
consts.comment: the tech ladder, the fusion rung: fusion power, commercial spacecraft, laser weapons, genetic engineering, and intercontinental governments at 18 (printed p. 52, Table 4).

consts.name: delTechRobotMin
consts.comment: the tech ladder, the robot rung: sentient robots and computers, solar power, and portable nuclear power at 19 (printed p. 52, Table 4).

consts.name: delTechFtlMin
consts.comment: the tech ladder, the FTL rung: faster-than-light space travel, matter transmission and replication, and interplanetary governments at 20; the low end - tools unknown and fire unharnessed at 2, stone at 3, copper at 4-5, iron at 6 (printed p. 52, Table 4).

consts.name: delAdvancedTechMagicMargin
consts.comment: the advanced-tech rule: sufficiently advanced technology works just like magic - an item whose technological rating exceeds the local technological rating still works if it also exceeds the local magical rating by at least five; steam engines require local T15 or higher or M10 or lower (printed p. 53).

consts.name: delEcologyHazardMax
consts.comment: the hazard band: worlds rated E6 or less inflict one or more of the table effects upon visitors from the base campaign, the type reflecting the environment's nature (printed p. 53).

consts.name: delEcologyParadiseMin
consts.comment: the paradise band: worlds rated E18 or higher seem paradises to visitors from E12 or less - with optional perils (the sleep until attacked, the flower's confusion-like euphoria with its singing and dancing) (printed p. 54).

consts.name: delEcologyNativeIntoleranceMin
consts.comment: the native-intolerance band: natives of worlds rated E16 or higher cannot tolerate less benign worlds (printed p. 54).

consts.name: delNativeSevereGap
consts.comment: the native intolerance, severe: E16+ natives suffer severe-condition effects on worlds rated five less than their home worlds (printed p. 54).

consts.name: delNativeHostileGap
consts.comment: the native intolerance, hostile: hostile penalties on worlds rated six less than home (printed p. 54).

consts.name: delNativeDeadlyGap
consts.comment: the native intolerance, deadly: deadly penalties on worlds rated seven or more less than home (printed p. 54).

bools.name: delChronoLocalityDoctrine
bools.comment: the chronological locality doctrine: characters are governed by local time wherever they are - a year on a C2 world ages the visitor a year while less than a minute passes at home; spell durations are local too (10 rounds on C11 is 10 rounds on C2 or C20); the flow always seems normal, even inside closed extra-dimensional spaces (portable holes, bags of holding, rope trick), with the shift imperceptible though clues appear (the noon portal into moonlit night) (printed p. 47).

bools.name: delMagicCastingTimeDoctrine
bools.comment: the low-magic casting-time doctrine: low-magic worlds impose a x2 to x5 multiplier on casting times; an adjusted casting time of 10 or more requires full rounds - 10 completes at the end of the round it began, 20 at the end of the second round; the odd remainder completes the next round at that initiative modifier (the fireball at 3 on an M6 world: adjusted 12, one full round, done in the second at modifier 2) (printed pp. 47-49).

bools.name: delMagicModificationDoctrine
bools.comment: the spell-modification doctrine: spells are modified by enhancement (one level higher, never on M9 or lower), diminution (one level lower), nullification (common on M9 or lower, rare on Prime worlds rated M10+ but frequent on highly magical outer planes and demiplanes), and alteration - superficial (the steam fireball), minor (the clairaudience ears with the save penalty vs. sound), or catastrophic (the berserk summons, the meteor swarm on the caster); natives often immune, PCs can learn the precautions; the Limbo Intelligence check negates any failed spell (printed p. 49).

bools.name: delPriestPlanarDoctrine
bools.comment: the priest planar doctrine: four world classes - open (lose levels by divine distance; all Outer Planes), closed (cast memorized but regain nothing above 2nd; many Prime worlds, pockets, demiplanes), restricted (all spells lost; very rare), unrestricted (full power; the Astral, Ethereal, and all known Inner planes); deities treat their focus Prime worlds as home; granted abilities generally function at full power by agreement, local conditions prevailing (no flame strike on the Plane of Elemental Water); divine agreement can circumvent the world's magical rating entirely (printed pp. 49-50).

bools.name: delPspDoctrine
bools.comment: the psionic doctrine: psionicists suffer less than spellcasters - the energies are personal and travel with the character; on M13+ worlds unaffected, on M9 or less the powers work but PSP costs rise for both initiating and maintaining; insufficient PSPs bar the power; local conditions never increase damage dice, duration, or range - increased cost is never an advantage (printed pp. 51-52).

bools.name: delItemDecayDoctrine
bools.comment: the item decay doctrine: items trace the shortest possible path home (unlike priest spells); an inert item still functions as its normal self (an inert suit of magical armor is still armor) and keeps its magical aura for detect magic, reviving when conditions improve; the cloak +3 example - full power across the Prime, +2 in the Astral or Ethereal, +1 on any Outer or Inner plane (printed p. 52).

bools.name: delMagicItemFunctionDoctrine
bools.comment: the item-function doctrine: as portable containers of power, items often function on low-magic worlds where their effects cannot be cast (the staff of the magi producing wall of fire on an M3 world); but a modified school reaches its items too (the catastrophically altered conjuration making Bucknard's everfull purse and a bag of tricks dangerous); stored spells and items bypass the spell-level bars (printed pp. 48, 52).

bools.name: delNaturalSpellcastingDoctrine
bools.comment: the natural spellcasting doctrine: intelligent natives of high-magic worlds cast naturally in the three bands, retained when visiting lower-rated worlds (with extended casting times and the high-level bars still applying); the abilities add to class abilities freely - the M20 fighter casts in metal armor, the M20 wizard still shuns armor but may enjoy extra spells or priest casting (printed pp. 50-51).

bools.name: delMajorRaceDoctrine
bools.comment: the major-race doctrine: a major race dominates its world as humans and demihumans dominate standard campaigns (the tanar'ri of the Abyss, the githyanki of the Astral); members native to high-magic worlds always have spell-like abilities in the three tiers, subject to local modifications - but natives always ignore their home world's detrimental effects (printed p. 52).

bools.name: delTechNotesDoctrine
bools.comment: the technological notes doctrine: sample items appear when affordable or in common use (the T5 algebra inventor working alone; not every T17 resident owns a jet, but they are in general use); devices from low-tech worlds work anywhere, but devices from high-tech worlds carried low go inert if they have moving parts, circuitry, or depend on chemical reactions - the T16 flashlight dies on a T8 world, the stainless steel ax still chops but loses its rust resistance, and a club is a club everywhere (printed p. 53).

bools.name: delEcologyDoctrine
bools.comment: the ecological doctrine: E2 is completely hostile, E20 a paradise, 10-12 generally earthlike with hazardous extremes (deserts, ocean depths, high-altitude thin air); the E6-or-less effects are the DM's choice reflecting the environment (the acidic atmosphere damaging, the polluted air draining Constitution); severe conditions allow mundane precautions (a desert or polar cap), hostile conditions threaten immediately (arctic water, volcanic gases - minor protective magic negates: endure cold/heat, ring of fire resistance, ring of warmth), deadly conditions kill within minutes (the lunar surface, a volcano's interior), and the listed deadly effects are minimums - the Plane of Elemental Fire demands a save vs. breath weapon or death, 5d10 damage even on a success (printed pp. 53-54).

bools.name: delQuirkDoctrine
bools.comment: the quirk doctrine: quirks are essential, serendipitous, or imposed - possibly changeable by the PCs; the infusion force twists everything (Ravenloft's evil bars all alignment detection and corrupts effects and psionics; on a Prime world it is temporary, removable by destroying the source); the conjuration bar (Athas - metal cannot be permanently created, the wall of iron falls to pieces); the named-spell bar (Melf's minute meteors unknown unless imported or researched from scratch); the dominant-race retaliation (possible only on M14+, leaders detect and retaliate against magical or psionic attacks - spell turning, the venomous insects per point of damage, the random spell); and the distance-immune world (items ignore planar distance, usually unrestricted) (printed pp. 53-54).

tables.name: delChronoBaseMag
tables.comment: the Table 2 grid (printed p. 46): 17 rows, ratings C2-C20 with the 10-12 band as one row; column 1 the base-campaign time MAGNITUDE, column 2 the UNIT code (1 second, 2 minute, 3 hour, 4 day, 5 week, 6 month, 7 year) - one week of local time equals the base time shown; the fast rungs 2-9, the typical band, the slow rungs 13-20.
col_comments: the Table 2 base-campaign time magnitude, by rating row (the fast rungs 2-9, the typical band 10-12, the slow rungs 13-20; one week of local time equals the base time shown).
the Table 2 unit code: 1 second, 2 minute, 3 hour, 4 day, 5 week, 6 month, 7 year - the unit of the base-campaign time magnitude.
the Table 2 rating, the row key: the campaign-time rating C2 through C20, the 10-12 band carried as one row keyed 10.

tables.name: delMagicRating
tables.comment: the Table 3 grid (printed pp. 46-47): 17 rows, ratings M2-M20 with the 10-12 band as one row; column 1 the RATING (the 10-12 band carries 10), column 2 the highest spell level castable (0 on dead-magic M2), column 3 the casting-time and PSP multiplier (0 on M2 where nothing functions), columns 4-5 the range of schools of magic modified (0-0 where none); the creature-size and demihuman bars ride the note consts.
col_comments: the Table 3 rating, the row key: the magic rating M2 through M20, the 10-12 band carried as one row keyed 10.
the Table 3 highest spell level castable at the rating (0 on the dead-magic M2 row).
the Table 3 casting-time and PSP multiplier (0 on M2 where nothing functions).
the low end of the range of schools of magic modified (0 where none are modified).
the high end of the range of schools of magic modified (0 where none are modified).

tables.name: delEcologyRollCount
tables.comment: the Table 5 grid (printed p. 54): three conditions at three intensities; column 1 the ROLL COUNT, column 2 the DIE SIZE (0 where no die is rolled - the poison save row), columns 3-5 the PERIOD codes for severe, hostile, and deadly (1 day, 2 hour, 3 round); the poison save is one saving throw at the end of each exposure period, failure immediate death; the deadly effects are minimums.
col_comments: the Table 5 roll count for the condition (the number of dice rolled; 0 where no die is rolled - the poison save row).
the Table 5 die size (0 where no die is rolled - the poison save row is one saving throw at the end of each exposure period, failure immediate death).
the Table 5 severe-condition period code: 1 day, 2 hour, 3 round.
the Table 5 hostile-condition period code: 1 day, 2 hour, 3 round.
the Table 5 deadly-condition period code: 1 day, 2 hour, 3 round - the deadly effects are minimums.

table_checks.note: the C2 world ages a visitor a year while under a minute passes at home (the fast end of the Table 2 grid)
the C20 world: one local week equals a hundred base years (the slow end of the grid)
the M8 world bars the 9th level and doubles casting times
the dead-magic M2 world: nothing functions
the typical M10-12 band: everything works, no school modifications
the deadly ecology: the constitution drain runs per round
the poison save row rolls no dice, one save per period
